decisions.finding: 'Forget the curve': the assistant's report will draw a ROC chart and I will not know what I am looking at
decisions.reason: Reading the output is the skill being taught, and one sentence is what SPEC rule 1 allows a secondary point. No thumbnail: the visual types have no slot for one.
decisions.change: Seg 7: 'Forget the curve' removed; after the meaning and the 0.85, one sentence: 'If a report draws the curve, hugging the top left corner is good and the diagonal is the coin flip.' The quote's sub line names the ROC curve and the glossary gains the term.

rulings.R4: Seg 9 is 45 words: size the list by capacity and judge any rival at that size, then the pointer to 2-4. Visual kept.
rulings.R5: Keyed longest in 2 of 10 (was 7). Two 'nothing' options replaced (2-3-q2 'None: ...', review 1 variant 2 'Nothing: ...'); review 1 variant 3's 'Nothing changes' reworded to the misconception it stands for; review 2 variant 3 keeps 'Neither changes' because it is the keyed answer. Two distractors were arguably right and are replaced: 2-3-q4 'use two cut-offs at once' (the lesson's own other-ways card recommends two cut-offs and three bands) is now 'flag only advertisers who clear both cut-offs', which is just the 0.5 cut-off; review 1 variant 2 'the rule's list cut down to its 300 biggest accounts' was itself a same-size comparison.
rulings.R6: Not triggered: the most usable move (sort by score and take as many as the team can handle) is the lesson's main spoken move in segs 4 and 8. Seg 8 left byte-identical.
rulings.R7: The four audit items were already checkable from the output (each figure names its cut-off or list size; model and baseline at the same number flagged; a random-list count on every top-K row; AUC beside the top-of-list numbers). Left as they were.
